summary: Rebecca Sundén works in Indology and Tibetology. She studied at the University of Hamburg, where she is attested in 2026 holding a post as a Wissenschaftliche Projektmitarbeiterin.

Reginald A. Ray is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He studied under teachers including Mircea Eliade, Charles H. Long, and Chögyam Trungpa, and held posts at the University of Colorado Boulder and Naropa University.
Reginald Edward Enthoven (1869–1952) was a scholar in history, archaeology, and Indology. He was educated at Wellington College from around 1883 to 1887 and entered New College in 1887.

Reginald Heber (1783–1826) was an Indology and religious studies scholar. He studied at Brasenose College (M.A. 1800) and the University of Oxford (~1800–1823, D.D.), becoming a Fellow at All Souls College, Oxford, in 1805.

Reginald Stephen Copleston (1845–1925) studied at Merton College and Exeter College, Oxford (B.A. 1864–1869). A scholar of Buddhist and religious studies, he was a Fellow at St John's College, Oxford (1870–1875) and President of the Royal Asiatic Society of Sri Lanka (~1880–1902).
Rei Yoshimura (b. 1929) is a scholar of Buddhist studies, history, and archaeology. He studied at Waseda University from circa 1949 to 1953 and served as a professor there from circa 1974 to 2000.
Reiho Masunaga (1902–1981) was a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar. He studied under Kaiten Nukariya (~1924–1934) and served as a teacher at Komazawa University from circa 1930 to 1972.

Reiko Ohnuma specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. She studied at UC Berkeley and the University of Michigan (Ph.D. attested 1997 under Luis Oscar Gómez) and held posts at UT Austin, the University of Alabama, and Dartmouth College.

Reimon Yuki (1902–1992) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo under Daijō Tokiwa. He held posts at the Academy of Oriental Culture, Kyoto Women's University, Ryukoku University, and the University of Tokyo.

Reiner Wiehl (1929–2010) was a philosophy scholar who studied at the University of Nancy and Goethe University Frankfurt. He served as Professor of Philosophy at the University of Hamburg (1969–1977) and Heidelberg University (appointed 1977).

Reinhold F. G. Müller (1882–1966) worked in Indology, history, and archaeology. He studied at Berlin, Innsbruck, and Greifswald (Dr.med.), later serving as an assistant at Greifswald (~1909–1911) and PD in medicine at Leipzig (1942).
Reinhold Grünendahl is an Indology scholar who held positions at the Free University of Berlin (attested 1983–1984) and the Göttingen State and University Library (attested 2008).

Reinhold Klotz (1807–1870) was a scholar in linguistics, history, and archaeology. He completed his Habilitation at the University of Leipzig, where he served as assistant professor (1832) and later as außerordentlicher Professor (1849–1870).

Reinhold Niebuhr (1892–1971) was a religious studies and philosophy scholar. He studied at Elmhurst University, Eden Theological Seminary, and Yale Divinity School, later serving on the faculty at Union Theological Seminary from circa 1928 to 1960.

Reinhold Rost (1822–1896) was an Indologist and linguist who earned his Ph.D. at Jena under Gildemeister and Stickel. He served as Secretary of the Royal Asiatic Society, Professor at King's College London, and Librarian at the India Office.

Reinhold Trautmann (1883–1951) was a linguist who earned his Ph.D. at Königsberg. He held professorships at the German University in Prague, Königsberg, and Leipzig, later chairing Slavic philology at Jena and heading the GDR Academy of Sciences.

Reinhold von Stackelberg (1860–1907) specialized in Iranian and Central Asian studies and linguistics. He studied at Tartu, Leipzig, and Strasbourg (Ph.D.), later serving as Privatdozent at Leipzig and Professor of Persian at the Lazarev Institute.
Reirin Yamada (1889–1979) was a Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at Komazawa University and later served as president of Komazawa Junior College from circa 1968 to 1974.
Remeen Firoz is an Indologist who, as of 2026, is a PhD student at the Australian National University studying under the doctoral supervision of Assa Doron.
Rena Aronovna Aulova (1927–1997) was an Indology and linguistics scholar. She studied at the National University of Uzbekistan (~1944–1949), where she later served as a Docent in 1979.
